I am an old woman now, 71 years, and my strength is not what it was, but this maize plot has fed my family for many seasons here on the slopes of Kilimanjaro. I keep a few cattle, so I spread their manure on the field before the rains come, and I plant beans and pumpkins between the maize rows as my mother taught me. I buy a little DAP and urea from the shop when I can afford it, but only a small amount because the prices are high, and I save seed from the best cobs of last season though sometimes I buy a bag of hybrid from the agrodealer in town. My grandchildren and my son help me weed and harvest, and during planting and weeding I pay two or three young men from the village to help because my back cannot bend like before.
